title: Measuring jug and a timer for an optional home tap-flow measurement (guide in the pupil PDF)
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Enlargement and similarity; ratio and proportion; rates
source: Written for mathematics/y9 lesson 68 (Measuring jug and a timer for an optional home tap-flow measurement (guide in the pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 68: Rates: flow, pay and unit conversions. A practical to do at home with an adult nearby. Read it all first.

practical.aim: To measure the rate of flow of a tap and the water used in wudu
safety: Do not waste water: use the water you collect for plants
An adult knows what you are doing and is nearby
Clear a space and tidy up afterwards; wash your hands
method: Turn the tap on to the flow you use for wudu
Hold the jug under the tap and start the timer
Stop the timer when the jug reaches 1 litre
Repeat twice and find the mean time
Rate = 1 litre ÷ time (in litres per minute)
Time how long the tap runs during one wudu and find the water used

questions.q: 12 litres per minute in litres per second
Big question: how do you compare rates given in different units?
questions.a: Convert them to the same units first, then compare the numbers.

questions.q: 1 litre takes 12 seconds. Find the rate in litres per minute.
At 5 litres per minute, the tap runs for 40 seconds. How much water is used?
